correctness.rationale: An Alexander-dual face forbids a disconnected induced triple, equivalently its induced complement graph has maximum degree ≤1. For every missing pair at cyclic distance d in (p,2p], the common-neighbor set has 2p−d+1 consecutive vertices spanning a clique; pairs at d≥2p+1 have none. Thus any face has a unique missing pair, and the lower/upper near-pair cone matching ordered by descending remaining dimension supplies actual free-face elementary collapses. The remainder is Cl(C_n^p) plus n(n−4p−1)/2 far chords, with Cl(C_n^p)≃S¹ for n>3p. The result is a wedge of 1+n(n−4p−1)/2 circles, and integral Alexander duality gives H_{n−4} of the original cut complex with no other reduced homology. Independent direct forbidden-triple scans at (p,n)=(2,9),(2,11),(3,13),(4,17),(5,21) confirmed common-neighbor clique and near/far counting; the global collapse is proved by matching, not finite tests.
